Question: Who is your favorite stormtrooper from the star wars franchise (Finn is allowed)?
Old_Answer: My favourite Stormtrooper is from the Expanded Universe, and was the original inspiration for the Darktroopers, as seen in The Mandalorian. Long before Moff Gideon and his Imperial Remnants unleashed the Darktrooper droids on baby Grogu, their was a General in the Imperial Army who firstly had the idea of cybernetically enhanced suits for his stormtroopers. Rom Mohc was a decorated war hero of the Clone Wars, then turned hero of the Empire after the fall of the Republic. He eventually overseen production of the revolutionary Dark Trooper Project. This top secret project was developed to create the ultimate evolution for the standard Stormtrooper. Below; Darth Vader himself gives his approval at General Mohcs work. The Empire had already designed a Darktrooper soldier, resulting in the Phase Zero Darktroopers, which were more a macabre zombie version of a Stormtrooper. It's purpose was to produce a soldier that had all the on field skills and initiative of a clone commando, coupled with the immense firepower of a B-Series Battle Droid. They eventually evolved into the Phase 1 and 2 versions of the Stormtrooper suit, but Phase 3 was something else entirely. Above;(from left to right) Darktrooper Phase I, Phase II, and Phase III. Using remnants left over from the technology that transformed Anakin Skywalker into a cybernetic monster the Empire concieved cybernetic warriors, who initially were clone veterans. This was the initial phase,..but by the time the project had gone into its third phase of suit development and design, the latest Phase III Darktrooper exosuit was classified as a ‘bipedal tank’. Above; General Rom Mohc in his own Phase III Battle suit. General Mohc even had a colossal, customised variant of his own. Not many of these hulking battle suits were produced, but the final glorious result was a mechanical monster, standing at over 2 and a half metres tall. A Stormtrooper to instil dread and fear into the heart of the Rebel Alliance. It boasted an impressive weaponry complement consisting of an overkill arsenal of rocket launchers, missiles, laser canons, frag grenades, thermal detonators and worse. This behemoth became a mobile weapons platform, created by the Empire to eradicate the Rebel pestilence permanently. Above; One Phase III Darktrooper crash landed on Tatooine, and was trapped there for three years, creating havoc for the locals; especially Jabba's swoop gangs. The outer shell of the Darktroopers extremely durable robotic exterior was made from the nearly indestructible material, Phrik, which could withstand a lightsaber strike. Skywalker would have shit his pants after realising his blade was virtually useless against one of these these Imperial wrecking balls. Above; Phase III Battle Suits ready for operation, standing in front of their forebears. Under General Mohcs command a squadron of stormtroopers, decked out with these nightmarish exosuits, slaughtered every single Rebel Alliance member during the bloody massacre of the Attack on Tak Base. Needless to say a high ranking Rebel agent defeated the good general shortly afterwards destroying not only Mohc but a valuable Imperial ship. This incident irrevocably led to the shutdown the Imperial Project, until Moff Gideon and his Imperial scientists discovered the problem with the suit was always the trooper. Below; the attack on Tak Rebel Base by Phase III Darktroopers. Could you just imagine being one of the terrified Rebel troopers at the base, seeing one of these giant mechanoid monstrosities pour out of lingering smoke of your grenade..as you realise that your fate is sealed? The fear, fury and destructive capabilities produced by these revolutionary exosuits makes these guys my pick for favourite Stormtrooper today.

His character arc is astonishing, evolving from a faceless, brainwashed soldier of the First Order to a self-aware, courageous individual who ultimately chooses the right path. His journey symbolizes the struggle against indoctrination and the power of choice, a theme that resonates deeply throughout the saga. When we first meet Finn in The Force Awakens, he’s grappling with the horrors of his past, particularly the atrocities committed by the First Order. The moment he chooses to drop his weapon and save Poe Dameron instead of following orders is not just a turning point for his character but a significant commentary on the nature of free will. Finn’s ability to question authority, defy expectations, and forge his own identity makes him relatable and compelling. Furthermore, his camaraderie with Rey and Poe adds an extra layer of depth to his character; it showcases the importance of friendship in overcoming darkness and adversity. Not to mention, his humor and charm provide a refreshing contrast to the more stoic characters we often see in the franchise. Ultimately, Finn represents hope and redemption, proving that even those who start as mere cogs in a machine can break free and fight for what they believe in. It’s this journey of self-discovery that makes Finn one of the most memorable stormtroopers, if not the most significant character, in the Star Wars universe.

When Grievous was known as Qymaen Jai Sheelal there is also the mention of his great grandmother who fought in a great war between their Kaleesh species, and the Bitthaevians at the Invasion of Guetica. She also served alongside a group of Jedi who firstly aligned themselves with Grievous’ people. During the war she used a Czerka Outland Rifle to help liberate her people, and in time this family heirloom was passed down to Grievous’ grandfather who taught the 9 year old Qymaen to become a demigod amongst his people with the weapon. When Qymaen matured and took the name Grievous after losing the love of his life to vicious insectoid invaders known as the Huk, or Yam'rii, he fought a brutal campaign against them and routinely returned home wounded from the battle. After his shuttle crash San Hill bought in Grievous’ remaining wives and children, and with this the former Kaleesh Warlord took a mask that resembled his fathers death mask,…and began his immense hatred towards the peacekeepers who had willingly doomed his people. Question: What was the reason behind the Kaminoans creating clone troopers?
Old_Answer: The Kaminoans were businessmen, specialising in making clones. This was what they did. The amphibious locals of Kamino had been pioneers in cloning and genetic engineering, ever since the end of an ice age that forced them to abandon their homes and live in enormous domed cities high above their flooded world. They were known to be extreme isolationists, and kept to themselves, but only to conduct business if it was profitable. They adapted their own genetic code in order to survive the great cataclysm of their world, and in doing so became experts in the field of cloning. They created clones and related technology for various clients across the galaxy, and those that knew of their business ventures, like Dexter Jettster, were aware that you had to be very financially secure to conduct said business with them. After taking the order from the Jedi, for a clone army for the Grand Army of the Republic, the Kaminoans considered the clonetroopers to be their most triumphant achievement. They had recieved the genetic material for the clone template from a bounty hunter named Jango Fett, who had been chosen because of his incredible proficiency in combat and despatching Jedi. After the first 200,000 clones had reached maturity Fett stayed on board with the Kaminoans, and assisted them with training the first generation of ARC troopers at Tipoca City. The Kaminoans played a crucial role in ensuring security for the planets of the Republic with their clone troopers, and recognised that their crowning achievement had been pivotal in opposing the onslaught of the Separatist Alliance. Kamino wasn't the only planet that had clone producing facilities, with a previous facility on Bora Vio being maintained until the major production facility on Kamino was established. The reason behind creating the clonetroopers for the Jedi was strictly business,..until the Empire had no further use for doing business between them; and terminated all existing and future contracts with the Kaminoans.

Old_Answer: One thing that Disney did to the sequel trilogy, that annoyed the crap out of me was the fact that they ditched a load of old alien species that we were all familiar with, and replaced them with their own new aliens and creatures. Maz Kanatas Castle on Tokadana for example is loaded with new alien species to the point where I didn't even recognise a single one! How can we have 6 episodes of the saga lined with alien species that are common in our minds, and then begin the sequel trilogy full of new species we've never seen before. Sure, a few new species here and there wouldn't be uncommon, but if you completely replace them then there's something deeply wrong with the folks who created the sequel trilogy. Take the scenes at the Casino on Canto Bight as another example. As you scan your eyes around the bustling crowd on the casino floor you can't help but notice that they're nearly all new editions to the saga. The only species I thought I could identify was the table attendant, with his tiny little croupiers outfit on, who I first thought was a Zilken like Colonel Meebur Gascon from The Clone Wars,..but as it turned out he was another new addition as well;..a Troglof to be specific. Almost every other character, besides an Ithorian I think I spotted, is of a species unfamiliar to the saga at the time, which to myself doesn't make a lot of sense. Why isn't there one familiar species, besides humans, that we can identify in these two immense scenes full of characters? Don't get me wrong, I enjoy the addition of some of the new alien species and characters, as they continue with the charm of Star Wars and new species being introduced,..but I feel that had Disney included more of the common and familiar species we know then it possibly could have added more value, charm and credibility to the film. Later productions like Solo, Rogue One, The Mandalorian, and Kenobi were more successful in this regard, with the inclusion of species like Twi'leks, Gamorreans, Rodians, Pau’ans, Trandoshans, Ithorians and even Jawas by the truck load. They even had familiar characters and cameos. But in the sequels I feel they went overboard on bringing new too many new species into the saga, without including some of our favourites to add more appeal. Look, my gripe is small compared with most other people's opinions on the sequels;..but I guess when I look at the bigger picture, like killing off my beloved Admiral Ackbar,..and some of the dialogue like “Palpatine somehow returned” didn't do the sequel trilogy justice neither.

Furthermore, the treatment of legacy characters, particularly Luke Skywalker, is frustratingly inconsistent. One moment he is the optimistic hero we grew up with; the next, he’s a jaded hermit who has lost faith in the Force.
